status_summary: DoD issued a class deviation on 2025-02-07 directing contracting officers to stop using project labor agreements on large-scale construction, the VA issued a similar deviation on 2025-02-20, and GSA issued a class exception for land port of entry projects. On 2025-05-16 the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia preliminarily enjoined the DoD and GSA memoranda in North America's Building Trades Unions v. Department of Defense. OMB Memorandum M-25-29 of 2025-06-12 stated that Executive Order 14063 remains in effect, that blanket deviations are precluded and earlier deviations should be rescinded, and that the administration supports project labor agreements when practicable and cost effective, while widening the cost and competition exceptions. An August 2026 CRS In Focus describes the order and its FAR rule as still in place. No Davis-Bacon repeal action was found.

timeline.event: DoD issued a class deviation directing contracting officers to end the use of project labor agreements on large-scale construction projects.
The VA issued a FAR class deviation memorandum barring project labor agreements on large-scale construction projects.
The U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia preliminarily enjoined the DoD and GSA memoranda in North America's Building Trades Unions v. Department of Defense (No. 1:25-cv-01070).

OMB Memorandum M-25-29 stated that Executive Order 14063 remains in effect, that blanket deviations prohibiting project labor agreements are precluded and earlier deviations should be rescinded, and revised the cost and competition exceptions.

title: End mandatory project labor agreement requirements on federal construction
uncertainties: The court order and the agency deviations were not opened; their dates and terms come from the American Bar Association, Economic Policy Institute and Government Executive accounts, which agree. Whether the injunction case was later resolved or mooted by the rescission of the deviations was not found. The CRS In Focus of 2026-08-12 (date from its file name) does not discuss the 2025 agency actions; it reports a separate Eleventh Circuit challenge to the order, affirmed against the challengers in April 2026 and pending on a rehearing petition. A September 2026 FAR overhaul proposal was noted by the researcher but not read. The Mandate presents this item as an alternative view, so alignment is partial.
